lede: The biggest thing on the civic calendar this week is Wednesday's BOCC meeting, where San Miguel County takes up two Land Use Code amendments — one governing natural medicine businesses and one reshaping rules around nonconforming lots, the kind of quiet code language that has real consequences for what gets built where. That same day, HARC holds public hearings on the large-scale Carhenge redevelopment at 700 W Pacific Ave, and the county kicks off its sixth working session on the Land Use Code rewrite focused on workforce and affordable housing zoning.
